comments.text:
As a 24-year-old West Palm Beach native, this video really hit home. A lot of people don't realize that Palm Beach and West Palm Beach have a deeply intertwined history. Before Palm Beach became known for its grand estates and luxury hotels, many of the Black laborers who built them lived in a settlement on the island called the Styx. They built the roads, bridges, mansions, hotels, and much of the infrastructure that turned Palm Beach into what it is today.

As the island grew wealthier, the Styx was dismantled, and many of its residents were forced to leave. Historical accounts describe homes being demolished or burned as the settlement was cleared. Many families relocated to segregated communities on the mainland, including Pleasant City in West Palm Beach. Imagine helping build one of the wealthiest communities in America, only to be told you couldn't live there once the work was done.

My family's history is tied to Pleasant City, so this isn't just something I read about—it's part of my family's story. Coming home from school over the years, I've watched South Florida change so rapidly that it sometimes feels unfamiliar. More development, more traffic, and less of the natural Florida I grew up with. It's heartbreaking watching farmland and ecosystems disappear while we increasingly rely on imported tropical fruit, even though South Florida is one of the few places in the continental U.S. where many of those crops can thrive. Florida has an incredible history, and I hope we do a better job preserving both the stories of the people who built it and the land that makes it so unique.
